title: Middlebury vs Wesleyan: tuition, size, location
summary: Middlebury College (Middlebury) versus Wesleyan University (Wesleyan). Also searched as Wesleyan vs Middlebury. Scorecard table is sourced; prose is checked against those facts. UniRepository is not affiliated with either school.

sections.heading: How they differ
paragraphs: Wesleyan University and Middlebury College are both private nonprofit institutions, as indicated by their ownership code 2 in the College Scorecard. Wesleyan University, located in Middletown, has an undergraduate enrollment of 3,067 students, while Middlebury College in Middlebury enrolls 2,738 undergraduates. Tuition costs also differ slightly, with Wesleyan charging $70,342 for in-state tuition compared to Middlebury's $67,600. These distinctions highlight differences in size, location, and tuition between Wesleyan University vs Middlebury College.

sections.heading: Cost
paragraphs: When comparing cost, Wesleyan University and Middlebury College have similar tuition rates for both in-state and out-of-state students. Wesleyan University charges $70,342 for tuition regardless of residency status, while Middlebury College's tuition is slightly lower at $67,600. Regarding student debt, the median debt for graduates who completed their programs at Wesleyan is $17,000, whereas Middlebury's median debt completers owe $13,857. These figures provide insight into the financial commitments associated with attending each institution, reflecting modest differences in tuition and graduate debt between Wesleyan vs Middlebury.

sections.heading: Pick Wesleyan if
paragraphs: Pick Wesleyan if you prefer a private nonprofit institution with a relatively low admission rate of 16.49%, indicating a selective admissions process. These factors make Wesleyan a suitable choice for students seeking a rigorous academic environment with a commitment to student success when considering Wesleyan University vs Middlebury College.
